intended_object: For a local ring R and a ringed space X, the canonical bijection between ring maps R → Γ(X, O_X) and ringed-space morphisms X → Spec R whose underlying continuous map is constant at the closed point. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (motivated by Vakil, Exercise 7.2.G).
explanation:
The forward map sends α to `hom R X α`. The base of that morphism is the constant map to the closed point. Its sheaf component on ⊤ is α, transported through the iso Γ(Spec R) ≅ R. On every other open it is the unique map into the terminal ring of sections over the empty set. This works because, in Spec of a local ring, the only open set containing the closed point is the whole space, so every proper open pulls back to ∅.

The inverse map takes the sheaf component of the morphism on global sections, composed with the iso `globalSectionsIso`. The proofs (`hom_globalSectionsMap` and `ext`) show that the two maps are mutually inverse. So this is exactly the expected classification: a morphism with fixed constant base is determined by, and can be built from, an arbitrary ring map R → Γ(X).

The setting is natural. Locality of R is what the construction actually needs: it is what forces every proper open to pull back to ∅. X can be an arbitrary ringed space, and R and X sharing the universe u is required by `Spec.sheafedSpaceObj`. Mathlib has the Γ–Spec adjunction for locally ringed spaces, but nothing for this non-local construction with constant base, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
